title: New Novaspace forecast: 6,500+ EO satellites to launch by 2035
summary: Over 6,500 Earth observation satellites are projected to launch by 2035, generating $155.9 billion in manufacturing revenues due to increased government demand for sovereign intelligence and surveillance capabilities.

title: Elve qualifies millimeter-wave amplifiers for spaceflight
summary: Elve, a California-based startup, has qualified its 100-watt millimeter-wave Traveling Wave Tube Amplifier platform for spaceflight. The qualification was supported by U.S. Space Force Small Business Innovation Research funding.

title: What’s next for ISR in space
summary: SpaceNews correspondent Debra Werner hosts a panel discussion on the future of Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (ISR) in space. The session explores emerging trends and challenges in this domain.

title: Moog Highlights Huntsville Expansion and New Hardware-in-the-Loop Lab During Space and Missile Defense Symposium
summary: Moog Inc. announced a major expansion at its Huntsville, AL facility, including a new secure Hypersonic/Interceptor Hardware-in-the-Loop (HWIL) lab. The announcement was made during the Space and Missile Defense Symposium.

title: Rock West Composites® Is Premiering Its New STRATOPultrusion™ Product Line at the 2026 Small Satellite Conference
summary: Rock West Composites is showcasing its new space-grade STRATOPultrusion™ product line at the 2026 Small Satellite Conference in August. The event will take place in Salt Lake City, Utah.

title: LatConnect 60 selects Transcelestial’s Space Optical Network for SWIRSAT imaging constellation
summary: LatConnect 60 has partnered with Transcelestial to use its Space Optical Network for the SWIRSAT-1 mission, enabling optical communications for the imaging constellation. This collaboration highlights advancements in space-based data transmission technology.

title: Draper Selects Proteus Space for Advanced On-Orbit Mission
summary: Proteus Space has been selected by The Charles Stark Draper Laboratory for an advanced on-orbit mission. This collaboration highlights Proteus Space's role in providing rapid, end-to-end access to space.

title: Moog Inc. Expands METEORITE Satellite Bus Capacity for High-Maneuverability Missions
summary: Moog Inc. has expanded the capacity of its METEORITE satellite bus to support high-maneuverability missions. This development enhances the platform's capabilities for precision motion and control systems in space applications.

title: Eoptic, Inc. Selected to Supply DeepScan™ Imaging Payloads Scheduled for Launch in 2027
summary: Eoptic, Inc. has been chosen to supply DeepScan™ imaging payloads for a launch scheduled in 2027. The company specializes in advanced multi-spectral and multi-modal imaging systems.

title: The 77th International Astronautical Congress (IAC 2026) is the One Space Event You Cannot Miss
summary: The 77th International Astronautical Congress (IAC 2026) is highlighted as a must-attend event for the global space community. The IAC has been a key annual gathering for over 75 years.

title: What happens when a galaxy's supermassive black hole turns off? These dying radio galaxies could show us
summary: Astronomers discovered a new population of galaxies with fading radio lobes, showing the aftermath when a galaxy's supermassive black hole stops feeding. This reveals what happens to these vast outflows when their black hole engines stall.

title: Trump signs new national space policy to enable 1,000 US rocket launches per year
summary: The U.S. has updated its national space policy to enable over 1,000 rocket launches annually by 2030, aiming to boost the country's spaceflight and reentry capabilities.

title: 'Star Trek: Strange New Worlds' cast talks losing sleep, living up to their character's legacy, and learning to ride a horse for season 4 (interview)
summary: The cast of 'Star Trek: Strange New Worlds' discusses the grueling schedule, high expectations, and unique challenges like learning to ride a horse for season 4. They highlight the physical and mental toll of producing the show.

title: Trump to award NASA's Artemis II astronauts the Congressional Space Medal of Honor
summary: NASA's Artemis II astronauts will receive the Congressional Space Medal of Honor on August 28. The award is given by former President Trump.

title: Japan unveils Mars moon sample-return spacecraft ahead of Oct. 19 launch (photos)
summary: Japan unveiled its MMX mission spacecraft, which aims to collect samples from Mars' moon Phobos and return them to Earth. The mission is scheduled to launch on October 19.

title: SpaceX fires up Starship ahead of megarocket’s 1st orbital flight (video)
summary: SpaceX conducted a single-engine test-firing of its Starship spacecraft to prepare for its first orbital test flight. This marks a significant step toward the megarocket's maiden orbital mission.

title: 'Dark stars' could be the seeds of supermassive black holes, scientists say
summary: A mysterious hum of gravitational waves in the cosmos may be linked to 'dark stars' that acted as seeds for supermassive black holes. Scientists suggest these long-dead stars could explain the origin of these cosmic giants.

title: SpaceX launches 29 Starlink satellites, lands rocket on ship at sea (video, photos)
summary: SpaceX successfully launched 29 Starlink satellites into orbit from Florida's Space Coast and landed the rocket on a ship at sea. This marks another successful deployment of broadband satellites for SpaceX's Starlink constellation.

title: Ancient stars dazzle in a celestial chandelier | Space photo of the day for Aug. 21, 2026
summary: The Chandelier Cluster, a celestial formation of ancient stars, was featured as the Space Photo of the Day on August 21, 2026. The image showcases the cluster's dazzling star arrangement resembling a chandelier.

title: On this day in space! Aug. 21, 1914: Total solar eclipse expedition crashed by WWI
summary: A total solar eclipse expedition planned for Aug. 21, 1914, was disrupted by the outbreak of World War I. The event highlighted the challenges of scientific exploration during wartime.

title: Ship 41 Completes Engine Testing Ahead of Flight 14
summary: Ship 41 has completed engine testing in preparation for Flight 14. Ship 40 is being transported back to Starbase from Christmas Island.

title: Stoke Space conducts second stage fit checks, completes first stage engines ahead of Nova debut
summary: Stoke Space has completed second stage fit checks and first stage engine development for its Nova rocket, aiming for a potential debut in 2026. This comes as the company advances its fully reusable vehicle amid competition in the space industry.

title: Zhuque-3 Completes Second Flight with Successful First-Stage Landing
summary: Zhuque-3, a methalox rocket developed by LandSpace, successfully completed its second flight and achieved a first-stage landing. This milestone marks a significant advancement for the company in reusable rocket technology.

title: Ship 40 arrives at Christmas Island, Plans Return to Starbase
summary: SpaceX has successfully guided Starship Ship 40 to a location off the coast of Christmas Island. The company plans to return the ship to Starbase for further operations.

title: Launch Preview: Chang’e 7 headlines week of Chinese and Starlink launches
summary: China is preparing for the Chang'e 7 lunar mission following a recent launch failure of the Chang Zheng 7A rocket. The upcoming week also includes multiple launches, including Starlink missions.

title: Firefly promote next block of Alpha amid Eclipse progress
summary: Firefly Aerospace is advancing its next-generation medium-lift rocket while also making progress on the Eclipse program. The company is promoting its next block of Alpha rockets amid these developments.

title: Blue Origin overviews plan for dual pad ops at Cape Canaveral
summary: Blue Origin is planning dual pad operations at Cape Canaveral as it restores its primary launch pad at LC-36A. The company has shared details about its operational expansion plans.

title: Rocket Lab advances via series of announcements
summary: Rocket Lab has established a new subsidiary in Germany and introduced a containerized mobile launch system. These moves mark the company's expansion and innovation in launch capabilities.

title: Amid failure, Wenchang celebrates milestone as China launches AI satellites and prepares for lunar south pole mission
summary: China's Wenchang Space Launch Site celebrated its 50th launch milestone while also facing a failure, as it launched AI satellites and prepared for a lunar south pole mission.

title: Starbase Production lining up future vehicles
summary: SpaceX's Starbase production site is advancing the assembly of multiple Starship vehicles for future missions. Teams are actively progressing through the production process at the facility.

summary: No specific news content was provided for analysis.

title: ESA Delivers: 50 years booklet
summary: ESA celebrates 50 years of achievements with a commemorative booklet highlighting 50 major milestones. The publication reflects on the agency's history and contributions to space exploration.

title: Phoenix 3: concept study for a reusable European spacecraft
summary: Engineers from ESA and industry partners completed a concept study for Phoenix 3, a reusable spacecraft for microgravity experiments and safe Earth return.

title: Proba-3’s eclipse hours before totality in Europe
summary: Proba-3 mission will create an artificial solar eclipse hours before the total solar eclipse in Europe. The mission aims to study the Sun's corona by blocking out the Sun's bright disk.

title: A double eclipse for Proba-3
summary: Proba-3, a space mission, captured a double eclipse where the Moon crossed its field of view. This event highlights the mission's precision in observing celestial phenomena.

title: How ESA mimics and models the 2026 total solar eclipse
summary: ESA is preparing to study the 2026 total solar eclipse by using artificial eclipse missions and computer simulations to observe the Sun's corona. This effort is crucial for advancing solar science despite the rarity and brevity of natural eclipses.

title: Your chance to run software in deep space on ESA's asteroid mission
summary: The European Space Agency is inviting European researchers and companies to run their software aboard the Hera mission, which will travel millions of kilometers into deep space. This offers a unique opportunity to test innovative software in a real deep-space environment.

title: From drone flight to sounding rocket
summary: A student-developed radar retroreflector technology was tested for the first time using a drone at ESTEC, the European Space Agency’s technical center in the Netherlands. The payload was carried during a drone flight, marking a step toward sounding rocket applications.

title: Earth and Proba-3’s Coronagraph play hide and seek
summary: ESA's Proba-3 mission will use a coronagraph to observe the Sun's corona by blocking the Sun's disk, simulating an eclipse. The mission involves two satellites playing a 'hide and seek' game to achieve this.

title: Meet space startups at ESA’s Industry Space Days
summary: ESA's Industry Space Days event on September 16-17 will showcase innovative space startups and foster collaboration with Europe's space industry. The event aims to exchange ideas, discuss opportunities, and highlight capabilities.

title: Letara Raises ¥2.6B to Build its Hybrid Rocket Engine Tech
summary: Japanese propulsion startup Letara raised ¥2.6B ($16M) in a pre-Series A funding round to develop its low-cost hybrid rocket engine technology.

title: SpaceWERX Announces 2026 STRATFI Awardees
summary: Space Force announced the 2026 STRATFI awardees through SpaceWERX during the Fed Supernova conference. This marks a key funding initiative under the SpaceWERX Strategic Funding Increase program.

title: Op-ed: The Technologies That Could Define the Future of Space
summary: Daniel Biedermann, a partner at NewSpace Capital, shares insights on key technologies shaping the future of space tech. The op-ed highlights emerging innovations that could redefine the industry.

title: Muon Space Raises $250M Series C
summary: Muon Space has secured $250 million in a Series C funding round to expand its satellite production capacity and diversify its mission capabilities.

title: Portal Books Dedicated Falcon 9 Amid Constrained Launch Market
summary: Portal Books a dedicated Falcon 9 launch while collaborating with Maverick Space Systems to sell the remaining fairing space for rideshare opportunities in a constrained launch market.

title: SpaceX’s Mobile Ambitions: Build, Partner, or Buy?
summary: SpaceX is exploring strategies to compete with major telecom providers like AT&T, T-Mobile, and Verizon by expanding into mobile services. The company aims to leverage its satellite and launch capabilities to tap into a multi-billion-dollar revenue opportunity.

title: White House Publishes S&T Strategy for National Security
summary: The White House released its National Security Science & Technology Strategy through the Office of Science and Technology Policy. This strategy outlines priorities for leveraging science and technology to enhance national security.
company: White House Office of Science and Technology Policy

title: Zeno Power Books its First Nuclear Mission to the Moon
summary: Zeno Power has secured its first commercial payload agreement with Firefly Aerospace to send a radioisotope heating unit to the Moon by 2028. The mission aims to demonstrate Zeno's technology for keeping a 5W device operational in lunar conditions.

title: Deep Dive: FY27 Defense Space Budget
summary: The U.S. Space Force's FY27 budget request has been highlighted as a record-breaking $71.3 billion. This budget request has drawn significant attention in the space industry.

title: Slingshot’s Portal Adds New AI-Powered Missions
summary: Slingshot Aerospace enhanced its Portal platform with AI-powered missions to improve monitoring of the increasingly crowded space environment. The update aims to assist operators in managing satellite traffic and space debris more effectively.

title: Fireside Chat with German Space Command: Featuring Major General Michael Traut
summary: A fireside chat features Major General Michael Traut, Commander of the German Space Command, discussing Germany's military space operations and efforts to protect space assets. The event highlights the integration of space capabilities into military strategies.

title: White House Targets Support for 1,000 Launches Per Year by 2030
summary: The White House announced a goal to support over 1,000 space launches and reentries annually by 2030 through a new National Security Presidential Memorandum. This initiative aims to bolster U.S. space industry capabilities and national security.

title: The Evolution of the Space Edge With Voyager CTO Paul Tilghman
summary: The article discusses the evolution of spaceborne computing, focusing on the shift to the 'space edge' rather than orbital data centers. It features insights from Voyager Space's CTO, Paul Tilghman.

title: Starcloud Adds $250M to Series A at a $2.3B Valuation
summary: Orbital data center startup Starcloud raised an additional $250 million for its Series A round, increasing its valuation to $2.3 billion just five months after the initial raise. The funding round was led by Manhattan West.

title: Space Norway Appoints Rune Jensen as Acting CEO With Morten Tengs Departure
summary: Space Norway has appointed Rune Jensen as Acting CEO following Morten Tengs' departure at the end of August. The company will now search for a new permanent CEO.

title: Sypris Electronics Wins Manufacturing Deal to Support LEO Constellation
summary: Sypris Electronics secured a manufacturing contract to produce power processing units for an unnamed Low-Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite constellation. The deal supports the development of next-generation satellites.

title: Muon Space Raises $250M Series C to Build Large-Scale Constellations
summary: Muon Space secured a $250 million Series C funding round to expand its large-scale satellite constellation development and enhance mission capabilities. This investment will accelerate the company's growth in the space industry.

title: Phantom Space Names Worth Wray as COO
summary: Phantom Space has appointed Worth Wray as its chief operating officer to oversee day-to-day operations and business scaling. The appointment aims to enhance operational efficiency and capital formation as the company expands.

title: Rocket Lab Launches SAR Satellite for Japan’s iQPS
summary: Rocket Lab successfully launched a synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite for Japan's iQPS on August 21 from New Zealand. This marks Rocket Lab's ninth launch for the Japanese company.

title: Rocket Lab’s Bold Move to Acquire Iridium: Analysts Break Down the Strategy
summary: Rocket Lab announced plans to acquire Iridium, marking a significant move in the satellite sector. Analysts are dissecting the strategic implications of this acquisition.
